2026-08-16.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new function pte_folio() that returns the folio mapped by a present page table entry (PTE). The function is intended to be used in conjunction with the existing pte_page() function, which returns the page mapped by a PTE. The patch converts several callers of page_folio(pte_page()) to use pte_folio() instead, and adds the new function to the Linux kernel's mm.h header file. This change is part of a larger effort to improve the handling of anonymous memory in the kernel, specifically for the anonymous collapse engine.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concerns that pte_folio() may be misused outside of hugetlb code, suggesting that vm_normal_page()/vm_normal_folio() or pte_page() should be used instead. He noted that most code does not need this helper and that its use is likely limited to hugetlb.
reviews.raw_body:
There is a reason why most code doesn't need that: because they should be using
vm_normal_page() / vm_normal_folio(), or need the exact page and handle special
ptes differently (see gup.c that uses pte_page()).

And other code that uses pte_page() doesn't really operate on folios AFAIKs.

That's also why you are only touching hugetlb code here.

IOW, there must be a pretty good reason for us to add a non-hugetlb helper when
that looks like a good fit for common code when it's really only hugetlb that
does weird things (and doesn't need the exact page!).

If we really *need* this helper, we should spell out clearly that it is very
likely the wrong thing to use outside hugetlb code.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested that the patch be submitted separately from the rest of the series, and noted potential benefits for future clean-up in get_user_pages code.
reviews.raw_body:
Oh nice, this could clean up some things in the
get_user_pages code too, when we get around to
tech debt there.

This could probably go in by itself.

Reviewed-by: Rik van Riel <riel@surriel.com>


-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo expressed concern that assuming every PTE has a folio is problematic, and suggested that using pte_page() as an arch-helper for low-level operations may be more appropriate.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm also a bit concerned about softleaves here. Kinda implying every pte
has a folio is problematic in general especially if there is nothing
guarding against that being used incorrectly.

pte_page() is more of an low-level arch-helper it seems to me (let's go
look up a PFN from the vmemmap modulo arch stuff around the pte).

So yeah I'm a little iffy about it too! :)

reviews.author: Rik Riel
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that copy-on-write (COW) can create 'holes' in a large folio, meaning __access_remote_vm() will still need to look up both the page and folio, and suggested this issue is not addressed by pte_folio().
reviews.raw_body:
Ugh, indeed. COW can create "holes" in the middle of
a large folio, so even __access_remote_vm() will
continue to need pages.

I guess we'll continue to look up both page and
folio in that code, then :/

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function pte_folio() to the Linux kernel, which returns the folio mapped by a present page table entry (PTE). The function is designed to simplify code and prepare for future changes related to anonymous memory management. It replaces existing calls to page_folio(pte_page()) in two files: fs/proc/task_mmu.c and mm/hugetlb.c. The patch also adds documentation for the new function in include/linux/mm.h.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David noted that pte_folio() currently relies on page_folio() and will fail if pages are decoupled from folios, suggesting more GUP work is needed to support this change.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, and it will be more fun once we decouple pages from folios, because then a
page_folio() will be allowed to fail.

(more GUP work, including in GUP users, is required to support that)

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that pte_folio() does not fit the abstraction and agreed to drop it, but proposed an alternative approach by reworking vm_normal_*() functions to be predicates on page table entries.
reviews.raw_body:
Fair.  pte_folio() does not fit the abstraction as it stands, so I will
drop it.

I thought that maybe we can rework vm_normal_*() to be a predicate on a
page table entry, so if it returns true the caller can safely use
pxx_folio(). It would be a cleaner interface in my opinion.

vm_ops->find_normal_page() breaks the idea, though.  Xen (being the single
user of the vm_op) wants the special bit to indicate a custom translation
to the page here.  A bool cannot describe this.

Ugh..

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
